duel.rule1: Space administrators claim this seven-day event. Personal accounts with a verified email or phone can participate within their space, one active match at a time. Empty rooms close after 10 minutes.
duel.rule2: Pick four digits from 0–9; repeats and a leading zero are allowed. Lock your code within 60 seconds. Feedback only counts digits in the correct position. Four exact matches solve the code.
duel.rule3: Submit simultaneously in 30-second rounds, up to 30 rounds. A solver must wait for the opponent's same-round turn. Two same-round solves, or no solution after 30 rounds, is a draw. A timeout skips that turn; three consecutive missed turns end the match without rewards.
duel.rule4: Tiers follow the lower level: 10 at LV1, 20 at LV8, 50 at LV14. Agree within 90 seconds, then both contribute the tier amount. Insufficient points prevent starting. The winner receives both entries, the loser loses their entry, and a draw refunds both. Levels follow the balance; collected cosmetics remain. Growth points have no cash value.
duel.rule5: No first-match bonus or protection. Up to five scored matches daily; only the first match per opponent scores. Draws count too. If either player is over a limit, both play free practice with no point changes. Limits reset in Beijing time, using the entry confirmation date.
duel.rule6: Leaving, tier or setup timeout, inactivity, or event expiry refunds paid entries and uses no scoring slot. Navigating away does not pause the timer. The server settles expired rooms even when both players are offline. New rooms close 18 minutes before the event ends.

patterns.intro: Seven interactions, seven intentions. Not everything needs a drawer, and not every action needs confirmation.

patterns.actions.title: A sheet for decisions
patterns.actions.hint: A short list of explicit actions, a separate cancel row and red destructive actions. No long forms or content.

patterns.snackbar.title: A small chance to undo
patterns.snackbar.hint: Perform a recoverable action, then offer Undo. Its timer pauses on focus, hover and backgrounding.
patterns.snackbar.use: Removing a draft, unfavoriting or removing a local selection can use a Snackbar. Cloud deletion and account closure need real recovery support before offering Undo.
patterns.alert.title: A decision that deserves attention
patterns.alert.hint: State irreversible consequences and use an explicit verb. Outside clicks, Escape and incidental Enter presses cannot decide for the user.
patterns.alert.use: Used by final account deletion confirmation. Irreversible file deletion and group dissolution are candidates; ordinary saves and recoverable actions are not.
patterns.tour.title: Illuminate one step at a time
patterns.tour.hint: Highlight the real target, explain one action, allow Back and Skip. Never force a tour on every visit.
patterns.tour.use: Offer opt-in guidance on a first Square visit, keychain setup or calendar binding. Missing targets use a centered explanation rather than a misleading spotlight.
patterns.lightbox.title: Let the content take the stage
patterns.lightbox.hint: Reuse the existing photo viewer: the cream archive plate preserves metadata, with fullscreen immersion a tap away.
patterns.lightbox.use: Chat images, Square attachments and cloud photos share ImageLightbox / MediaLightbox, preserving zoom, downloads, metadata and navigation.
patterns.inline.title: Keep errors beside their input
patterns.inline.hint: Keep the explanation visible until corrected, then allow progress. A brief Toast is not form validation.
patterns.inline.use: Used by friend-search failures. Nicknames, invitation codes, OAuth callbacks and contact-binding fields can adopt persistent inline validation.

notification.guide.bark.1.title: Install and allow notifications
notification.guide.bark.1.body: Open Bark and allow system notifications when prompted.
notification.guide.bark.2.title: Copy your private push URL
notification.guide.bark.2.body: Copy the URL beginning with https://api.day.app. Sample text at the end is safe to include; FRIENDEN cleans it automatically.
notification.guide.bark.3.title: Send a test code
notification.guide.bark.3.body: Paste the URL, send a test, then return from Bark and enter the six-digit code.
notification.guide.ntfy.1.title: Install ntfy
notification.guide.ntfy.1.body: Use the App Store on iPhone. Android supports Google Play or the F-Droid build without FCM.
notification.guide.ntfy.2.title: Subscribe to a private topic
notification.guide.ntfy.2.body: Create a hard-to-guess topic and copy its full URL, such as https://ntfy.sh/your-topic. Add an access token only for protected topics.
notification.guide.ntfy.3.title: Confirm the test message
notification.guide.ntfy.3.body: Send a test code, confirm it arrived in ntfy, and enter the six digits here.
notification.guide.gotify.1.title: Install the client and prepare a server
notification.guide.gotify.1.body: Gotify needs a reachable server. Install the Android client and sign in to your Gotify server first.
notification.guide.gotify.2.title: Create an application token
notification.guide.gotify.2.body: In the Gotify web console, create an application dedicated to FRIENDEN and copy its application token, not a client token.
notification.guide.gotify.3.title: Verify the server and token
notification.guide.gotify.3.body: Enter the server root URL and application token, then confirm the test code in Gotify.
notification.guide.pushdeer.1.title: Install a suitable client
notification.guide.pushdeer.1.body: Search for PushDeer in the App Store on iPhone. Android users should review the project status first; self-hosted users can use their own client and server.
notification.guide.pushdeer.2.title: Register a device and create a PushKey
notification.guide.pushdeer.2.body: Sign in, register this device under Devices, then create and copy a PushKey beginning with PDU under Keys. Add your server URL when self-hosting.
notification.guide.pushdeer.3.title: Confirm delivery with a code
notification.guide.pushdeer.3.body: Send a test using the PushKey. Once the notification arrives, enter the six-digit code to finish.

bgm.rule1: The event lasts 30 days. Days follow Beijing time. Progress starts after joining; active days need not be consecutive.
bgm.rule2: Earn 6 for your first public post, 3 each for comments on 3 different posts by others, and 1 each for likes on 5 different authors. Maximum 20 daily.
bgm.rule3: Post once or comment on two different posts by others for an active day. Anonymous, friends-only, self-interactions and repeat actions do not count.
bgm.rule4: Get your first track on joining. One daily post collects all 12 in 15 days; comments and likes can shorten this to 10 active days (90 inspiration required). For example, one post, comment and like each day completes the collection in 10 days. Days need not be consecutive and existing progress is kept. Equip up to six tracks; earned tracks remain after the event.
